pk.context: 25 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

tell: Its parent half-life is only 1.4 hours, yet its metabolites persist for 13.8 to 16.5 hours.

clues.text: Food raises bioavailability by about 95.4%, and more than 90% is bound to plasma proteins. It is rapidly and extensively metabolized, with metabolites excreted mainly in the urine.
Molecular weight 416.6. It is practically insoluble in water but soluble in alcohol, and freely soluble in chloroform.
Tablets under an NDA, in 25, 50 and 100 mg strengths.
No boxed warning; contraindicated in hyperkalemia, Addison's disease and with concomitant eplerenone. Gynecomastia is the most common adverse reaction.
Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, add-on treatment of hypertension, and edema in cirrhosis or nephrotic syndrome.
Competitively blocks aldosterone receptors in the distal renal tubule, so sodium and water are excreted while potassium is retained.
The generic name begins with S and has fourteen letters.
